biography: Rafael Barranco, born in the bustling favelas of São Paulo, never forgot the roar of engines echoing from the Interlagos circuit. His father, a mechanic for a local karting team, instilled in him a love for speed and precision. Rafael's career began with pilfered parts and late nights in his father's garage, culminating in a surprise victory at the Brazilian Karting Championship at age 16. This win caught the eye of a junior formula team, launching him into the European racing scene. While promising results in Formula 3 and Formula 2 hinted at greatness, a series of unfortunate incidents and team changes stalled his progress. Now, driving for Gordini G.P., Barranco is determined to prove that his early potential was not a fluke. He's at a critical juncture, needing to convert raw speed into consistent results to secure his future in the sport. The weight of his nation, and his own aspirations, rests on his shoulders.
drivingStyle: Barranco's driving style is as fiery as his Brazilian spirit. He's known for late-braking maneuvers and an aggressive approach to overtaking. He extracts every last ounce of performance from the car, often pushing it to the very edge of grip. Tire management isn't his forte; he prefers an all-out attack, sacrificing longevity for immediate gains. Under pressure, Barranco tends to become even more aggressive, either resulting in spectacular victories or disastrous crashes. He thrives on the thrill of the chase, often making daring moves that leave spectators breathless.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud dating back to their Formula 3 days. Rossi accused Barranco of reckless driving, and the two have exchanged heated words both on and off the track.

Barranco and Dubois have clashed multiple times on track, their differing driving styles often resulting in collisions. Barranco sees Dubois as overly cautious, while she views him as a danger to the other drivers.
Tanaka beat Barranco to the F2 championship, and Barranco feels Tanaka only won because of superior machinery.

quirks: Always wears a small charm his grandmother gave him, hidden inside his racing suit.
Refuses to start a race without listening to a specific samba song.
Has a habit of talking to his car before each session, thanking it for its service.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I race to win, no matter the cost."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Grand Prix in his debut season, overtaking the championship leader on the final lap in front of his home crowd, is undoubtedly his greatest achievement.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the Monaco Grand Prix due to an unforced error, costing him a potential victory and severely damaging his team's morale, remains his most painful memory.
